friendly-nations.title: Friendly Nations Visa in Panama
friendly-nations.description: The friendly nations visa allows citizens of certain countries to obtain residency in Panama.

faq.question: How to obtain residency in Panama as a foreigner?
faq.answer: To obtain residency in Panama as a foreigner, you must apply under an immigration programme suited to your nationality and profile. The most widely used options include the Friendly Nations Visa, the Qualified Investor Residency, and the Retiree Visa. The Friendly Nations Visa allows you to obtain residency in Panama by demonstrating an economic or professional tie to the country. The Qualified Investor Residency requires a minimum investment of $300,000 USD. The Retiree Visa is designed for those wishing to live in Panama with retirement income from $1,000 USD per month. Residency in Panama requires apostilled documents and compliance with the requirements of the chosen programme.

faq.question: What are the requirements to obtain residency in Panama?
faq.answer: The requirements to obtain residency in Panama include a valid passport, apostilled criminal record certificate, and fulfilment of a valid immigration programme. Among the most commonly used residency programmes in Panama are the Friendly Nations Visa, the Qualified Investor Residency, and the Retiree Visa, each with specific conditions depending on the applicant's profile. Residency in Panama for foreigners varies by nationality or country of residence, as some programmes only apply to certain countries. Residency cannot be obtained with a criminal record or if the applicant appears on international control lists.

faq.question: How much does residency in Panama cost in 2026?
faq.answer: The cost of residency in Panama in 2026 depends on the visa type chosen, but in general legal and administrative fees for obtaining residency in Panama range from $5,000 to $10,000 USD per person. The Qualified Investor Residency requires a minimum investment of $300,000 USD, while the Panama Retiree Visa requires monthly income from $1,000 USD. The Friendly Nations Visa may involve variable costs depending on the economic or professional tie used. The price of residency in Panama varies by programme, the foreigner's profile, and the structure used to apply.

faq.question: How long does residency in Panama take?
faq.answer: The time for residency in Panama depends on the immigration programme. In most cases, obtaining residency in Panama takes between 3 and 6 months from submission of a complete file. The Qualified Investor Residency allows you to obtain residency in Panama within a legal timeframe of 30 days. In contrast, the Friendly Nations Visa in Panama typically takes several months due to administrative verifications. The Panama Retiree Visa follows timelines similar to the standard process. The time to obtain residency in Panama can vary depending on nationality, visa type, and proper preparation of the file.

sections.heading: Current Legal Framework
sections.body: The National Migration Service will receive your application under the program "Permanent Residence Permit for Citizens of Nations with Friendly, Commercial, and Professional Relations with Panama". This program, commonly known as the "friendly nations visa", was created by Executive Decree 343, dated May 16, 2012, and later modified by Executive Decree 197 of May 7, 2021. Note that since 2022, applicants first obtain a probationary permit for two years before they can apply for permanent residence.

sections.heading: Reasons for Applying
sections.body:
Three options are available to obtain Panamanian residence through the friendly nations visa:

  • Employment: A work contract from a legally established company on Panamanian territory is required. Obtaining a work permit is legally mandatory if this path is chosen.
  • Real estate: Purchase of a property with a minimum value of $200,000.
  • Bank investment: Maintaining an amount equal to or greater than $200,000 in a Panamanian banking entity for three years.

sections.heading: Main Documentation
sections.body:
• Legal representation by a lawyer.
  • Five passport-type photos and a notarized passport copy.
  • Criminal record from the country of residence.
  • Medical certificate.
  • Checks endorsed to Panamanian institutions.
  • Proof of the reason for the application (employment contract, assets, etc.).
  • For dependents: proof of family relationship and financial stability.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria
sections.body: Interested parties must possess citizenship from one of the nations considered friendly in commercial and diplomatic spheres with Panama. This extends to close relatives — parents, descendants, and spouses. If your country is not on the list, other alternatives are available — contact Panama Contact Services to study the best option for your personal situation.

digital-nomad.title: Digital Nomad Visa
digital-nomad.description: Short-stay visa for remote workers: up to 9 months, extendable for another 9, with foreign-source income of at least B/.36,000 a year.

faq.question: Can I work for a Panamanian company with this visa?
faq.answer: No. The visa authorizes remote work tied to a foreign company or clients abroad. It does not allow you to accept employment or provide services in the Panamanian market.

faq.question: Can I apply if I am self-employed?
faq.answer: Yes. You must show that your company is registered outside Panama and submit a sworn statement describing your clients, services, income and how you are paid.

faq.question: Do I need health insurance?
faq.answer: Yes. You must submit a policy that covers your stay in Panama for the requested period.

faq.question: Does the visa lead to permanent residency?
faq.answer: Not automatically. It is a short-stay visa within the non-resident category. If you want to settle in Panama permanently, you will need to review the residency options and their requirements separately.

faq.question: Can I apply from abroad?
faq.answer: Official information indicates that the applicant must have entered Panama and that the application is filed through a legal representative with the National Immigration Service. Nationals of restricted countries must first obtain the authorized entry visa, where applicable.

sections.body:
Panama offers a short-stay visa for foreigners who work remotely for a company or clients abroad. Commonly known as the Digital Nomad Visa, it allows you to stay in the country for up to nine months and to request an extension for another nine months. To qualify, the applicant must perform duties whose effects take place outside Panama and receive foreign-source income of at least B/.36,000 a year.

This visa can be an option for anyone who wants to spend a season in Panama while keeping their professional activity abroad. However, it is not permanent residency, and it does not authorize you to work for Panamanian employers, clients or companies. The official category is the Short-Stay Visa for Remote Workers, created by Executive Decree No. 198 of May 7, 2021.

sections.heading: Who can apply for the Digital Nomad Visa?
sections.body:
A foreign national who works remotely for a foreign company, or who is self-employed with clients abroad, can apply. The activity must be carried out remotely, its effects must take place outside Panama, and the income must come from a foreign source.

The minimum income requirement is B/.36,000 a year, equivalent to B/.3,000 a month, or the equivalent in another currency. Showing that you receive that amount is not enough: the documentation must make it possible to verify the employment or business relationship, the origin of the funds and how often payments are made.

An employee of a foreign company must have a letter from that company detailing their position, duties, salary, remote work arrangement and payment frequency. A self-employed applicant must show that their company is registered abroad and describe their relationships with clients and the services they provide. The activity and income must comply with the conditions of the visa.

sections.heading: How long does the visa last?
sections.body:
The visa is granted for a maximum of nine months and can be extended only once for the same period. The maximum stay under this category is therefore eighteen months, provided the extension is requested and approved under the applicable rules.

This is a non-resident immigration category. Obtaining it does not automatically grant permanent residency, nor does it change your immigration category by itself after the eighteen months. If you wish to remain in Panama after that period, you will have to leave the country or assess whether you meet the requirements of another immigration category and file the corresponding application.

sections.heading: What activities does it allow, and which are excluded?
sections.body:
Once approved, the visa allows you to work remotely from Panama for a foreign company or provide services to clients abroad, as long as the conditions that justified the application are maintained. The regulation provides that the holder may carry out this remote activity without obtaining an additional work permit for that arrangement.

The permit does not authorize you to accept a job offer or provide services in the Panamanian market. During the application, the applicant must sign a sworn statement declaring that they will not accept job offers or services in Panama in order to do business in the national territory. For that reason, this visa should not be used to join a Panamanian company as an employee or to serve local clients through an activity that generates Panamanian-source income.

sections.heading: What documents are required?
sections.body:
The application usually includes personal, immigration, employment and financial documents. The exact list should be confirmed before filing, since Immigration may update its forms or request additional documentation depending on each case.

The documents provided for include:

  • Notarized power of attorney and an application filed by a legal representative.
  • Three passport-size photographs and a duly certified copy of the passport.
  • Criminal record certificate legalized by apostille or through the relevant consular channel.
  • Health certificate and sworn declaration form on personal background.
  • Application form, which includes the commitment to cover return or repatriation costs if necessary.
  • Medical insurance policy covering Panama for the length of the stay.
  • Bank records showing that the income comes from abroad and is linked to the declared work or activity.
  • Sworn declaration of not accepting job offers or services in Panama.

If the applicant is an employee of a foreign company, they must provide a certificate of existence of the company and a letter on company letterhead signed by its legal representative. The letter must identify the applicant, describe their position and duties, confirm that they work remotely, state their income and payment frequency, and declare that the income comes from abroad. The company must also assume return or repatriation costs where applicable.

If the applicant is self-employed, they must provide proof that their own company is registered abroad. They must also provide a notarized sworn statement describing their business relationship with clients, the services they provide, the fees they receive, the origin of the funds and the frequency of payments. Documents issued outside Panama must meet the applicable authentication formalities and, if they are not in Spanish, must be translated according to current requirements.

sections.heading: How is the application filed?
sections.body:
The applicant must have entered Panama to start this procedure. The application is filed with the Special Procedures Window of the National Immigration Service through a legal representative. If the applicant’s nationality requires an authorized visa to enter the country, they must obtain it before traveling and then apply for this category.

Preparing the file is an important part of the process. Make sure the letters, certificates and bank statements match in terms of employer or clients, activity, income and payment frequency. A discrepancy between documents can lead to requests for correction or delays in the evaluation.

The Executive Decree provides for a payment of B/.250 to the National Immigration Service and a cost of B/.50 for the corresponding ID card. There may also be legal fees and costs for authentication, translation and obtaining documents. Before starting, confirm the applicable costs and current payment method with your legal representative.

sections.heading: Does the visa mean foreign income is automatically tax-free?
sections.body:
The visa should not be presented as an automatic tax exemption. Panama applies territorial rules to determine whether income is Panamanian-source or foreign-source, and the immigration category does not replace that analysis. The visa requires that the work produce effects outside Panama and that the income come from abroad; tax treatment depends on the nature of the activity and where its effects occur.

The Tax Authority (Dirección General de Ingresos) recognizes foreign-source income in its forms and tax materials. Even so, if you have doubts about your tax situation, review your contracts, where the services are used and how you receive payments with a tax advisor.

sections.heading: Does the visa let me stay longer than a tourist visa?
sections.body:
The permitted tourist stay can depend on your nationality, the category of entry and the authorization granted by immigration authorities. For that reason, it is not accurate to state in general that all European citizens can stay three months and all Canadians six. Panamá Digital states that tourist visas can be granted for up to ninety days, subject to international agreements and reciprocity rules. Before traveling, confirm the period that applies to your passport and check the authorized date of stay when you enter.

The Digital Nomad Visa is a separate category for remote workers who meet its requirements. You should not assume that you can stay in Panama as a tourist and start working remotely without reviewing the applicable immigration conditions. The application for this visa is processed after entering the country, but it should be prepared in advance and filed according to the established procedure.

sections.heading: Thinking of working remotely from Panama?
sections.body: Book a video call with us to learn the current conditions of the Short-Stay Visa for Remote Workers and review the documents you would need for your application: schedule an appointment with Panama Contact Services. You can also explore our immigration and relocation services in Panama.

qualified-investor.title: Qualified Investor Visa
qualified-investor.description: Permanent residency in Panama through investment: requirements, amounts and timelines in force in 2027.

faq.question: Is residency granted automatically when I invest?
faq.answer: No. The investment must fit an authorized route, meet the source-of-funds and documentation requirements, and be certified by the MICI. Migration must then rule on the residency application.

faq.question: Does the US$300,000 minimum still exist?
faq.answer: Yes, but not for just any property. It applies to new first-sale properties and to certain purchase promises that meet the decree’s conditions. For secondary-market properties, the minimum is US$500,000.

faq.question: Can I include my family?
faq.answer: The decree allows applications with dependents, subject to documentary requirements and additional payments. Eligibility and documents depend on the relationship and the situation of each family member. Confirm the current requirements before filing.

faq.question: Do I have to live in Panama permanently?
faq.answer: The category grants permanent residency, but it should not be confused with nationality or a guarantee of citizenship. For questions about absences, maintaining your status or naturalization, the immigration rules applicable to your case must be reviewed.

faq.question: Can I finance part of a property purchase?
faq.answer: The decree allows financing the amount above the minimum in certain circumstances, as long as the net computable value does not fall below the applicable threshold. The structure must be reviewed before signing.

faq.question: How long does the whole process take?
faq.answer: The rules provide for up to 15 business days for the MICI investment certification and up to 30 business days for Migration’s ruling, counted from the milestones set for complete files. Preparing the investment and documents may add time.

faq.question: When can I sell or withdraw the investment?
faq.answer: The investment must be maintained for five years, depending on the route. If it ceases to exist earlier, the decree sets out notification obligations and, under certain conditions, a period to replace it. Selling or withdrawing funds without reviewing these rules may put your immigration status at risk.

sections.body: To apply for permanent residency as a Qualified Investor, the minimum investment in force depends on the route: US$300,000 for a new first-sale property or a purchase promise that meets the decree’s conditions; US$500,000 for a secondary-market property, eligible securities, or a term deposit at Banco Nacional de Panamá or Caja de Ahorros; and US$750,000 for a deposit at an authorized private bank. The investment must come from your own lawful, traceable funds and be maintained for five years. Under Executive Decree No. 17 of 2026, in force since September 16, 2026, the MICI has up to 15 business days to certify a complete application and Migration up to 30 business days to rule on it, once the complete file is received. The category is aimed at foreigners making an investment admitted by the regulation; amounts and requirements depend on the route chosen.

sections.heading: What is Qualified Investor residency?
sections.body:
It is an immigration subcategory that lets you apply for permanent residency in Panama through an investment that meets the conditions set by the Government. The process has two main phases: obtaining certification of the investment from the Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI) and filing the residency application with the National Migration Service.

The rule in force is Executive Decree No. 17 of September 8, 2026, published in Official Gazette Digital No. 30613. It replaced Executive Decree No. 722 of 2020 and its amendments, which is why some websites still show earlier rules. To confirm which requirements apply to an application, consult the text of the decree in the Official Gazette and the programme information published by the MICI.

sections.heading: What are the routes and minimum amounts?
sections.body:
The programme covers real estate investments, investments in the Panamanian securities market and fixed-term deposits. The real estate route now distinguishes between first-sale properties and secondary-market properties.

RouteMinimum investmentMain condition
New first-sale propertyUS$300,000Must meet the decree’s first-sale conditions
Purchase promise (promesa de compraventa)US$300,000Must be structured under the conditions and guarantees provided
Secondary-market propertyUS$500,000The net computable value must reach the minimum
Eligible securities in the Panamanian marketUS$500,000Investment through a licensed securities firm
Term deposit at Banco Nacional or Caja de AhorrosUS$500,000Deposit placed directly at one of those banks
Term deposit at an authorized private bankUS$750,000Deposit at an institution with a general licence

For routes subject to a maintenance period, the investment must be kept for five years. The table summarizes the thresholds of the current rule; immigration, legal and third-party costs are paid separately.

sections.heading: What changed for real estate investment?
sections.body:
Since September 16, 2026, the minimum depends on the legal and commercial status of the property. For a new, unoccupied property acquired in a first sale from the promoter, developer or their successor, the minimum is US$300,000. For a property that has already been marketed, occupied, leased or transferred to an unrelated person, the minimum is US$500,000, subject to the decree’s conditions and exceptions.

It is not enough for a unit to look new or to have never been lived in by its current buyer. You must verify whether it meets the definition of first sale in the regulation. In addition, to calculate the amount that can be recognized, the accredited value is taken into account and any liens on the property are deducted. If there is a mortgage, the net value must still reach the applicable minimum.

In some cases, the authority may request an independent commercial appraisal. It is therefore wise to review the property’s status, the price, the purchase structure and the documents before signing or transferring funds.

sections.heading: Can I apply with a property under construction?
sections.body:
Yes. A purchase promise can support a residency application from US$300,000, provided it is structured as the decree requires. The options described include using a trust administered by an authorized entity or, under specific conditions, paying 100% of the price to the developer with a bank guarantee in favour of the investor.

Protection varies with the structure used. Before committing funds, confirm which mechanism your specific case requires, when the money will be disbursed and what happens if the project is never completed. The decree sets deadlines and conditions for replacing an investment that is not completed for reasons attributable to the developer.

sections.heading: What options exist outside real estate?
sections.body:
The securities route lets you invest at least US$500,000 in eligible Panamanian-market instruments through a licensed securities firm. The decree includes categories such as certain investment funds, instruments issued or guaranteed by the State, and corporate securities that meet the regulatory conditions.

You can also place a fixed-term deposit. The minimum is US$500,000 at Banco Nacional de Panamá or Caja de Ahorros, and US$750,000 at an authorized private bank with a general licence. The investment must meet the source, documentation and maintenance requirements that apply to the route.

sections.heading: Who can apply and how do I prove the funds?
sections.body:
The category is aimed at foreign nationals who make one of the admitted investments. The applicant may invest personally or, where the route allows it, through an entity in which they can prove they are the beneficial owner and control the investment.

The funds must be your own, lawful, traceable and from a foreign source, as set by the decree. You will need to document their path: where they come from, how they reached Panama and how they were used to complete the investment. If a company or foundation is used, you must also support its existence, good standing and ownership structure.

Permanent principal residency is not Panamanian citizenship and does not guarantee automatic naturalization. The decree regulates how naturalization applications are channelled and requires that the corresponding constitutional and legal requirements be met.

sections.heading: What are the costs and timelines?
sections.body:
Investment amounts do not include the government payments for the procedure, professional fees or third-party costs. For the main applicant, the decree provides for US$5,000 to the National Treasury and US$5,000 to the National Migration Service as a repatriation deposit. For each dependent, it provides for US$1,000 to the National Treasury and US$1,000 to Migration.

ItemAmount or timeline
Government payments, main applicantUS$10,000 in total
Government payments, per dependentUS$2,000 in total per person
MICI investment certificationUp to 15 business days from admission of the complete file
Migration rulingUp to 30 business days from formal receipt of the complete file
Maintaining the investmentFive years, depending on the route and its conditions
Professional fees and third-party costsVariable; should be quoted separately

Legal deadlines start when a complete file is admitted or received. They are not the total time needed to prepare documents, make the investment, handle translations, apostilles, appraisals or banking procedures. The MICI certification has a limited validity for filing with Migration; check its validity before submitting the application.

sections.heading: What are the steps to apply for residency?
sections.body:
1. Choose the route. Compare first-sale property, secondary market, securities or term deposit. Pick the option based on your investment goal and available capital.
  2. Verify eligibility before paying. For a property purchase, confirm in writing whether the property qualifies as first sale or secondary market, what value can be recognized and whether there are liens.
  3. Document the source of funds. Gather bank statements, transfer receipts and financial documents that explain the lawful origin of the capital and its path to the investment.
  4. Complete the investment and gather the supporting documents. Depending on the route, prepare registry, banking, securities, contractual or trust documents.
  5. Request certification from the MICI. File the complete application so the Ministry can review and certify the investment.
  6. File the application with Migration. With a valid certification, the immigration file is submitted, including personal documents and the corresponding payments.
  7. Maintain the investment and meet later obligations. Keep the investment for the required period and confirm how to prove it remains in place at each applicable review. If it must be replaced, respect the notification and reinvestment deadlines set by the decree.

The list of documents may vary by route, ownership structure and whether dependents are included. Book a video call with us to learn the current conditions of Qualified Investor residency and get your questions answered.

sections.heading: What mistakes should I avoid?
sections.body:
• Using amounts from an earlier rule. Decree No. 17 replaced the previous regime. In particular, the US$300,000 real estate minimum no longer applies generally to resale properties.
  • Assuming a never-lived-in property qualifies as first sale. The classification depends on the facts and documents of the transaction, not just the property’s physical condition.
  • Calculating the minimum from the advertised price. The recognized value may depend on the price paid, the accredited commercial value and any liens.
  • Sending funds without keeping a paper trail. Transfers without clear supporting documents can complicate the certification of the investment.
  • Confusing the repatriation deposit with legal fees. They are different items; ask for a breakdown of public fees, professional fees and third-party costs.
  • Waiting until the end to review the transitional rules. If the investment or binding contract was completed before September 16, 2026, you may be able to opt for the previous regime within the six-month transitional period. The date and eligibility must be confirmed for each file.

retiring.title: Pensionado Visa
retiring.description: Permanent residency for retirees and pensioners in Panama: lifetime pension from B/.1,000 a month, indefinite permit and benefits.

faq.question: Is pensioner residency temporary?
faq.answer: No. The rules provide that it is granted for an indefinite period and does not require renewal.

faq.question: Does the pension have to be lifetime?
faq.answer: Yes. The pension must be granted for life by a foreign government, an international organization or a private company.

faq.question: Can I apply with a B/.750 pension?
faq.answer: Yes, if you show that you purchased real estate in Panama in your own name worth more than B/.100,000. The rules then allow the minimum pension to be B/.750 a month.

faq.question: Can my spouse and I combine our pensions?
faq.answer: Yes. The regulations allow the pensions of both spouses to be combined to reach the general minimum, with documentation for each pension.

faq.question: Can children be included as dependents?
faq.answer: They can be included if they meet the applicable family reunification, age or study conditions. Confirm the specific requirement with Immigration before preparing their documents.

faq.question: Does the Pensionado Visa entitle me to discounts?
faq.answer: The visa and the discounts have different legal bases. Pensioner resident status may allow you to claim the benefits provided for retirees and pensioners by Law 6, subject to its requirements and proof of eligibility.

faq.question: Is there a minimum age to apply for residency?
faq.answer: The immigration rules consulted define eligibility by the lifetime pension and do not state a general minimum age of 25. The file must show that the pension meets the legal conditions.

sections.body:
A foreign national who receives a lifetime pension from a government, an international organization or a private company can apply for permanent residency in Panama as a retiree or pensioner. The general requirement is to show a monthly pension of at least B/.1,000. If the applicant has already purchased real estate in Panama in their own name worth more than B/.100,000, the minimum may be reduced to B/.750 a month. In addition, B/.250 a month must be shown for each dependent; spouses may combine their pensions to reach the minimum. The permit is granted indefinitely and does not require renewal, under Executive Decree No. 320 and its amendments.

It is important to distinguish this residency from retiree discounts: the visa is an immigration permit, while the discounts are governed mainly by Law 6 of 1987 and have their own requirements. Panamá Digital’s information summarizes the criteria published by the National Immigration Service.

sections.heading: What is permanent residency as a retiree or pensioner?
sections.body:
It is an immigration permit for foreign nationals who receive a lifetime retirement pension and wish to settle in Panama. The legal basis is Executive Decree No. 320 of 2008, amended, among other rules, by Executive Decree No. 26 of 2009. Article 203, as amended, provides that the permit is granted for an indefinite period without the need for renewal.

In everyday speech it is often called the “Pensionado Visa”, but the legal category is a permanent resident permit as a retiree or pensioner. The application must be filed through a legal representative with the National Immigration Service.

sections.heading: Who can apply for the Pensionado Visa?
sections.body:
A foreign national who receives a lifetime pension from a foreign government, an international organization or a private company, and who wishes to settle in Panama, can apply. The core requirement is that the pension is granted for life and reaches the established minimum.

The regulations reviewed do not set a general minimum age of 25 for applying for this permit. Eligibility is based on the pension and on the documents showing that it meets the legal conditions. For that reason, the age of 25 should not be presented as an official requirement of the visa.

If the pension comes from a private company, additional evidence about the company and the management of the funds may be required. The regulations mention documents from the pension administrator, trust, mutual funds, insurance or banking entity, as well as proof of payment or account statements.

sections.heading: What is the minimum income required?
sections.body:
The general minimum is a lifetime pension of B/.1,000 a month. The exception allows applying with a minimum pension of B/.750 a month when the applicant shows that they purchased, in their own name, property in Panama worth more than B/.100,000. This is not a rule that allows adding up any family-owned or company-owned property: the requirement published by Panamá Digital refers to the purchase of the property in the applicant’s own name.

Spouses may combine their pensions to reach the B/.1,000 minimum, provided both prove their income and submit the required documents. This option is provided for in the immigration regulations.

sections.heading: What conditions apply to dependents?
sections.body:
The application may include dependents, but each one must meet the applicable family reunification requirements. Panamá Digital’s page states that the documents required for the temporary resident permit by family reunification must be submitted. In addition, adult dependents must grant power of attorney themselves.

The pensioner must show additional financial solvency of B/.250 a month per dependent. The regulations allow this to be shown through an additional pension or a local bank reference. For dependent children, the National Immigration Service sets special conditions on age and studies; confirm the requirement in force for your case before gathering documents.

sections.heading: What documents are usually submitted?
sections.body:
The exact list depends on the family situation and the type of pension. The file usually includes:

  • Power of attorney and application prepared by the legal representative.
  • Copy of the passport, authenticated or certified in the manner accepted by Immigration.
  • Criminal record certificate.
  • Health certificate.
  • Sworn declaration form on personal background.
  • Official certification proving retiree or pensioner status and the amount of the lifetime pension.
  • Proof of additional solvency for each dependent.
  • Public Registry certificate for the property, if the B/.750-a-month exception is used.
  • Documents proving marriage or kinship, if family members are included.
  • For a private-company pension, additional documents on the entity that pays it and whoever manages the funds.

Documents issued abroad must be apostilled or authenticated, as applicable. If they are not in Spanish, Panamá Digital states they must be translated by an authorized public translator in Panama. Check the current list with the National Immigration Service before filing.

sections.heading: How much does the process cost and how long does it take?
sections.body:
The B/.100,000 real estate investment is only necessary if the applicant uses the exception that lowers the minimum pension to B/.750. It is not a requirement for those who show a lifetime pension of B/.1,000 or more.

Law 9 of 1987 provides tariff exemptions for pensioners, including the import of personal items and a vehicle, under the conditions of that law. It also establishes an exemption from certain immigration charges related to obtaining the visa. Professional fees, translations, apostilles and other costs of preparing the file are separate items.

  • Minimum lifetime pension: B/.1,000 a month.
  • Property exception: B/.750 a month if a property purchased in the applicant’s own name for more than B/.100,000 is shown.
  • Additional solvency per dependent: B/.250 a month per person.
  • Duration of the permit: indefinite, no renewal.
  • Processing time: the official sheet consulted does not state a single processing time.
  • Preparation costs: variable (fees, apostilles, translations and documents).

A fixed approval time should not be promised: preparation and review depend on the file being complete and on Immigration’s evaluation.

sections.heading: Are the Pensionado Visa and retiree discounts the same thing?
sections.body:
No. They are separate benefits governed by different rules. The Pensionado Visa grants permanent residency and is governed by immigration law. Discounts for retirees and pensioners are found mainly in Law 6 of 1987, whose consolidated text was published in the Official Gazette.

Law 6 covers Panamanians and resident foreigners aged 55 or over if women and 60 or over if men, as well as retirees and pensioners of any gender. A person who obtains residency as a pensioner may therefore be entitled to the discounts by virtue of their pensioner status, even if they have not reached the age that applies to those who qualify by age alone. To access each benefit, they must be able to prove the required status to the establishment or provider.

The current legal text consulted provides, among others, discounts of 50% on shows; 30% on intercity buses, trains, launches and boats; 25% on airfares and restaurants; 15% on franchise fast food and certain clinic services; and 20% on medicines and medical consultations. It also provides discounts on hotels, electricity, water and telephone, subject to conditions and limits. Not all percentages apply to all services or without limit.

In 2026, the National Assembly reported that a bill to modify benefits for retirees and pensioners had been approved in first debate. Initial approval of a bill is not the same as a law in force: before publishing new percentages, final approval, enactment and publication in the Official Gazette must be verified.

sections.heading: What import exemptions does the law provide?
sections.body: Law 9 of 1987 grants retirees and pensioners a full, one-time tariff exemption to import household or personal items up to B/.10,000. It also provides an exemption every two years to import a vehicle for personal or family use. These exemptions are customs benefits separate from the Law 6 discounts and are subject to their own conditions; confirm the procedure and documentation with the National Customs Authority before shipping goods or buying a vehicle.

sections.heading: Does the residency allow me to work in Panama?
sections.body:
No. Permanent residency as a retiree or pensioner lets you settle legally in Panama but does not grant a work permit. Whoever obtains this residency therefore cannot take a job, provide professional services or carry out work activities in the country under that immigration category.

This does not prevent you from holding shares or interests in a company, owning a business or serving on its board of directors. You may take part in shareholder or director meetings and exercise the rights that come with that corporate status. The difference is that being a shareholder or director is not, by itself, the same as working in the company: pensioner residency does not allow you to take on work duties or run the day-to-day operation of the business.

sections.heading: What mistakes should be avoided?
sections.body:
• Presenting B/.750 as an option without showing a property purchased in your own name for more than B/.100,000.
  • Confusing the B/.250 per dependent solvency with an immigration fee.
  • Assuming there is a minimum age of 25 without confirming it in the current rules.
  • Submitting foreign documents without apostille or authentication, or without an official Spanish translation.
  • Assuming that residency and discounts are a single automatic benefit.
  • Publishing new discount percentages based on a bill that has not yet completed the legislative process.
  • Confusing the Law 9 import exemption with the Law 6 discounts.

faq.question: How to create a company in Panama as a foreigner?
faq.answer: Creating a company in Panama as a foreigner is a fast process that allows you to open a company in Panama without needing residency. The most commonly used structures are the Sociedad Anónima (S.A.), the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (S.R.L.), and the Private Interest Foundation. The S.A. is the most widely used option for commercial activities and international investment. The S.R.L. is more commonly used for local operations. The Private Interest Foundation in Panama is used primarily for asset protection and estate planning. Opening a company in Panama is handled by a lawyer and allows a registered structure to be in place within a few days, even remotely in certain cases.

faq.question: What are the requirements to create a company in Panama?
faq.answer: The requirements to create a company in Panama as a foreigner include a valid passport, information about the intended activity, and compliance forms. To create a Sociedad Anónima (S.A.), a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (S.R.L.), or a Private Interest Foundation in Panama, it is mandatory to designate a resident agent and declare the beneficial owners. Residency is not required to open a company in Panama. Companies and foundations in Panama must comply with obligations such as the annual flat tax (tasa única) and maintenance of the resident agent.

faq.question: How much does it cost to create a company in Panama?
faq.answer: The cost of creating a company in Panama depends on the chosen structure. Creating a Sociedad Anónima (S.A.), a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (S.R.L.), or a Private Interest Foundation in Panama typically costs between $1,500 and $2,000 USD. Opening a company in Panama also involves annual costs such as the tasa única, the resident agent, and administrative services, which generally range from $600 to $1,000 USD per year. The price of a company or foundation in Panama varies depending on the foreigner's profile and the structure used.

faq.question: Can a foreigner buy property in Panama?
faq.answer: Yes, a foreigner can buy property in Panama with the same rights as a Panamanian citizen. The law allows foreigners to acquire real estate in Panama in their own name or through a company or foundation. Buying property in Panama as a foreigner is a safe process provided the property title is verified and the transaction is conducted correctly. It is not mandatory to have residency in Panama to purchase a property, but it may facilitate banking and administrative procedures.

faq.question: What are the requirements to buy property in Panama?
faq.answer: To buy property in Panama, a valid passport and a signed purchase agreement are required. In practice, due diligence is also necessary to verify that the property is free of encumbrances and correctly registered in the Public Registry. Buying real estate in Panama involves reviewing the legal history of the property, validating the seller, and correctly structuring the purchase, especially if it is carried out through a company or foundation.

faq.question: How much does it cost to buy property in Panama?
faq.answer: The cost of buying property in Panama includes the property price plus taxes and legal fees. The main costs are a 2% transfer tax on the higher value between the sale price and the registered value, and a 3% withholding on the sale value for capital gains tax. Legal fees, notary costs, and Public Registry inscription fees must also be considered. These costs vary by transaction but in practice typically amount to around 3% to 5% of the property value, depending on the structure and negotiation. The total cost may change if the purchase is made through a company or if the distribution of taxes between buyer and seller is negotiated.

faq.question: Can buying property in Panama lead to residency?
faq.answer: Yes, buying property in Panama can allow you to obtain residency, provided the investment meets the requirements of a current immigration programme. The Qualified Investor Residency allows you to obtain permanent residency in Panama through a minimum real estate investment of $300,000 USD, with a legal processing time of 30 days. It is also possible to apply for the Friendly Nations Visa, which allows you to obtain temporary residency through a minimum real estate investment of $200,000 USD or a bank deposit. This programme requires maintaining an economic tie to Panama and leads to permanent residency after the provisional period. Buying property in Panama is one of the most widely used ways for foreigners to obtain residency, as it combines real estate investment with immigration benefits.

faq.question: Who must file an income tax declaration in Panama?
faq.answer: Any individual or legal entity generating income in Panama must file an annual Income Tax Return (ISR). Individuals have until March 15th each year; legal entities until March 31st. Extensions of one month are possible but must be requested on time. Since 2022, gross annual incomes exceeding $11,000 USD require validation by a certified public accountant.

faq.question: What types of income tax declarations exist in Panama?
faq.answer: There are five types: a Normal Declaration (for employees, independent professionals, and traders), a No Operations Declaration (for taxpayers with no activity during the year), a Final Declaration (for businesses ceasing operations), an Original Declaration (filed for the first time), and an Amending Declaration (to correct previous submissions, subject to conditions and potential penalties).

sections.body: The Income Tax Return (ISR) is a document where individuals and legal entities report their income and expenses during a fiscal year in Panama. This declaration is mandatory annually for anyone or any entity generating income in the country.

sections.heading: Deadlines for Income Tax Declaration
sections.body: Individuals have until March 15th each year to submit their declaration. Legal entities must do so before March 31st. Extensions of one month are possible but must be requested timely to avoid penalties.

sections.heading: Types of ISR Declarations
sections.body:
Normal Declaration: For employed individuals, independent professionals, and traders.

No Operations Declaration: For taxpayers who had no activities or transactions during the fiscal year.

Final Declaration: For businesses that dissolve or cease operations.

Original Declaration: Submitted for the first time to declare income, expenses, and deductions.

Amending Declaration: To correct errors or omissions in previously submitted declarations. Subject to conditions and can lead to penalties if not made in time.

According to Article 81 of Executive Decree 98 of September 27, 2010, all taxpayers must submit a declaration. With the enactment of Law 280 of December 30, 2021, validation from a certified public accountant is required for gross annual incomes exceeding B/. 11,000.00.

sections.heading: First-Year Tax Declaration
sections.body:
It's important to differentiate between the tax declaration and the tax payment. The declaration is a document to be filled out and submitted online — based on the declared income and expenses, a payable tax amount may or may not be generated.

Consult a competent accountant familiar with the various types of declarations. The type of declaration to submit will differ based on the status or activity of the company or individual.

faq.question: Can I use my foreign driver's license in Panama?
faq.answer: Yes, but only if you are entering as a tourist. A valid foreign licence can be used for 90 days from your date of entry. However, as soon as you initiate a migration process in Panama, you are no longer considered a tourist and may not drive on a foreign licence — even if the 90 days have not elapsed. A $50 fine applies, and in the event of an accident, your insurance may not cover you.

faq.question: How do I get a Panamanian driver's license as a foreigner?
faq.answer: You have two options once you have migration status: homologation (exchanging your foreign licence) or starting from scratch with a Panamanian driving school certified by Sertracen. Documents not in Spanish must be officially translated. In many cases, retaking the test is faster and less costly than homologation.

sections.body: In the isthmus country, regulations to consider are established by "Sertracen", the agency responsible for regulating and supervising land traffic and transport. On the ground, the agents of the land transport authority (ATT) are often responsible for traffic regulation. If you enter Panama for the first time as a tourist with a valid driver's license from your home country, you can use it for 90 days from the date of entry.

sections.heading: ⚠️ Important Warning
sections.body: Initiating your migration process immediately prohibits you from using your foreign license in Panama. No longer a tourist, you no longer have the right to drive a vehicle on Panamanian soil, even if the 90-day period has not elapsed. You must wait to have a Panamanian driver's license to drive again. Besides a fine of $50, the police can immobilize your vehicle, and in the event of an accident, you may not be covered by your insurance.

sections.heading: Options After Obtaining Migration Status
sections.body:
Homologation (exchange): If you have a driver's license from your home country and want to exchange it. Documents not written in Spanish must be translated by an authorized interpreter in Panama. Often, it is faster and less costly to retake the driving test in Panama directly.

Starting from scratch: If you do not have a license or do not wish to homologate, you must attend a driving school certified by Sertracen. Panama Contact Services guides you through partner schools.

sections.heading: License Validity

Foreign licenses are valid for three months and allow driving under categories A, B, C, and D. Public transport driving is not authorized with these categories.

In Panama, the Panamanian license is issued for a period of four years. For foreigners with temporary or provisional status, the validity coincides with their residence card. Only permanent residents benefit from the full four-year validity.

life-quality.subtitle: Good Living
life-quality.shortDescription: Panama can offer connected city living, access to services and a wide variety of landscapes, but there is no single cost of living that applies to everyone.

sections.body: Panama can offer connected city living, access to services and a wide variety of landscapes, but there is no single cost of living that applies to everyone. INEC recorded a year-on-year CPI change of 2.8% in September 2026, while the annual change for 2025 versus 2024 was -0.1%. These are general price indicators, not a monthly budget for a family or for a foreign resident. To get your bearings, it also helps to look at specific services: the capital's public transport integrates the Metro and Metrobus, MINSA maintains a directory of health facilities and MEDUCA publishes information on schools. Panama can be a good option for professionals, families, retirees and remote workers, but the choice of city and housing changes the experience a great deal. Before moving, compare neighborhoods, rents, transport, healthcare and schools according to your personal needs.

sections.heading: What does a good quality of life in Panama mean?
sections.body:
Quality of life does not depend on a single figure. It includes your available budget, commuting time, access to healthcare, educational options, safety in the area where you live and proximity to activities and services. In Panama, these factors can vary considerably between Panama City, cities in the interior and coastal or rural communities.

The capital concentrates a larger supply of transport, medical centers, shops, restaurants and cultural activities. In other provinces, some people prioritize tranquility, closeness to nature or a slower pace, although there may be fewer transport options and specialized services. That is why choosing “Panama” as a destination is not enough: the practical decision is choosing where to live and which services you need nearby.

Natural diversity is an important part of the country's lifestyle. In a 2025 publication, the Ministry of Environment stated that the official forest cover map records 61.4% forest cover across the national territory. The same source highlights that Panama brings together terrestrial and marine ecosystems on two coasts. This richness lets you enjoy parks and natural areas, always respecting their access and conservation rules.

sections.heading: How much does it cost to live in Panama?
sections.body:
It is not responsible to sum up the cost of living in a single figure without knowing whether it is for one person or a family, whether you rent or buy, and whether you live in the capital or another region. INEC's consumer price index (CPI) data show how the prices of a basket of goods and services change over time; they do not tell you how much each household will pay for rent, school, health insurance or transport. Local income also matters when assessing cost. INEC's labor survey for August 2026 reported a national unemployment rate of 8.5% and an informality rate of 45.8% in non-agricultural employment. These figures do not determine a foreign resident's budget, but they are a reminder that purchasing power and working conditions vary widely between households.

The US dollar is in everyday use and the balboa is pegged one to one to the dollar. This makes it easier for many people to plan their spending if they already earn in dollars. However, it does not remove the need to budget: prices for housing, education, private healthcare, electricity and transport can vary depending on location and type of service.

Indicator or expenseAvailable official referenceHow to interpret it
Price changeYear-on-year CPI: 2.8% as of September 2026Measures the general change in prices, not a family's budget
HousingThere is no single national price describing all rentalsCompare properties by neighborhood, size, services and contract
Public transportIn 2026 the ATTT published student fares of B/.0.17 on Metro Line 1 and B/.0.25 on Line 2These are student fares with defined conditions and validity; they should not be taken as the general fare
HealthcareMINSA provides a public directory of facilities and servicesCheck which facilities and specialties exist near your chosen area
EducationMEDUCA publishes information on the school network and schoolsConfirm location, offering, availability, calendar and format directly with each school

The student fare cited by the ATTT was tied to the 2026 school benefit, valid from March 2 to December 11. It serves as a reference for one specific public fare, not as an estimate of an adult's monthly transport spending.

sections.heading: What are the infrastructure and transport like?
sections.body:
Panama City has integrated public transport with Metro and Metrobus lines. These options can be useful for people who live and work near their routes, but not all residential areas have the same access. Before renting or buying, locate the nearest station, check the routes you will need and estimate travel time at typical hours.

For road travel, the Pan-American Highway connects various parts of the country. However, the infrastructure is under constant maintenance and expansion. In 2026, the Ministry of Public Works reported rehabilitation work on sections of the Panamericana Oeste and works on the David–Viguí road. This may improve connectivity in the long term, but it also means travel times can be affected by roadworks, traffic or road conditions. Tocumen International Airport offers connections to regional and international destinations. For daily life, however, it is better to assess airport access and everyday mobility separately: being close to an airport does not necessarily mean having convenient transport to work, school or the doctor.

sections.heading: What are the healthcare and education options?
sections.body:
The public health system consists of facilities run by the Ministry of Health and the Social Security Fund (CSS), as well as private providers. The MINSA directory lets you look up health centers and facilities by location. In 2026, the Ministry announced an investment plan of close to B/.1 billion to build, rehabilitate and modernize hospitals, health centers and polyclinics in different regions. This is an announced plan to strengthen the network, not a guarantee that all services will be immediately available in every community.

Families moving with children should compare educational options well in advance. MEDUCA publishes information on the official system and authorizes the operation of private schools. Bilingual schools and international programs exist, but the offering, language, availability, calendar and costs vary from one institution to another.

sections.heading: Is Panama a safe country?
sections.body:
It is not helpful to describe the whole country as uniformly safe or unsafe. The experience changes depending on the province, district, neighborhood, time of day and personal routines. It is also important to distinguish between perceived safety and official statistics: crime figures describe reported and recorded incidents, but they do not replace an assessment of the specific place where you plan to live.

INEC publishes justice and crime statistics, which can be consulted as a national and territorial reference. Before choosing housing, it is prudent to walk the area during the day and at night, check the routes to work or school, ask about transport access and consult the authorities' recommendations. Remote areas and urban zones should not be assessed with the same generalization.

sections.heading: What does Panama offer for leisure and outdoor life?
sections.body:
A practical advantage of living in Panama is the variety of activities available: Pacific and Caribbean beaches, hiking, birdwatching, national parks and water activities. The Ministry of Environment manages protected areas and publishes information for visitors, including opening hours and access rules. Some areas require registration, an admission fee or prior arrangement, so it is wise to check the conditions before traveling.

Cultural and social life is also unevenly concentrated. Panama City offers museums, restaurants, events, shopping centers and business activities. In the interior, fairs, local festivals and outdoor activities may be more visible in everyday life. The Panama Tourism Authority reported that 1,755,998 international visitors arrived during the first half of 2026, and that the country hosted 74 international events between January and June. These are tourism activity figures, not a direct measure of quality of life, but they show the variety of events and services organized in the country.

sections.heading: How do you assess whether Panama fits your lifestyle?
sections.body:
Before making a decision, organize your assessment into concrete steps:

  1. Define your priorities. Decide whether you value public transport, access to hospitals, schools, nature, cultural life or tranquility most.
  2. Compare locations. Assess the capital, interior cities and coastal areas in terms of services, distances and connectivity.
  3. Prepare a personal budget. Include rent or mortgage, utilities, transport, food, healthcare, education and travel.
  4. Check the available services. Use the official MINSA and MEDUCA directories, and review transport routes and roadworks.
  5. Visit neighborhoods before committing. Walk around at different times of day and test the journeys you would make frequently.
  6. Consult recent official data. The CPI, labor indicators, safety statistics and sector publications can change; check the date of each figure.

sections.heading: What mistakes should you avoid when comparing quality of life?
sections.body:
• Assuming Panama is cheap for everyone. Spending depends on the housing, location and services you choose.
  • Using the CPI as if it were a budget. It is an indicator of price change, not a list of individual monthly expenses.
  • Confusing the student fare with the general transport fare. ATTT benefits have conditions and a validity period.
  • Choosing an area based only on photos or reputation. Check the surroundings, nearby services and daily journeys.
  • Taking for granted that medical or educational offerings are the same in every province. Review facilities, specialties, authorizations and availability.
  • Claiming that the whole country is safe or dangerous. Assess the official data and the conditions of each specific area.

sections.heading: What are the frequently asked questions from people considering a move to Panama?
sections.body:
Is it cheap to live in Panama?
There is no universal answer. INEC data let you observe price changes, but the budget varies depending on the city, the rent, household size and lifestyle.

Is the dollar Panama's currency?
The US dollar is in everyday use and is legal tender. The balboa is pegged one to one to the dollar, according to MEF information.

Can you live in Panama City without a car?
It depends on the neighborhood and your usual journeys. The capital has the Metro and Metrobus, but how comfortable it is to live without a car depends on proximity to stations, routes and the services you need.

Is there healthcare outside the capital?
Yes. MINSA maintains facilities in different regions. The availability of specialists, hospitals and specific services varies; check the official directory for the area you are interested in.

Are there bilingual and international schools?
MEDUCA publishes information on schools and regulates private schools. The availability of programs, languages, places and calendars must be confirmed directly with each institution.

Is Panama safe for families?
Safety depends on the area and the circumstances. Consult official statistics, visit the neighborhoods and assess specific routes and routines before choosing where to live.

sections.heading: Are you considering moving to Panama?
sections.body:
Quality of life also depends on choosing well where to live and preparing your move in good time. At Panama Contact we can guide you on residency, housing and other services to settle in the country. Book a free consultation to talk about your project.

Quality of life in Panama can be very different from one person to another. The best way to assess it is to compare the official figures with your real needs for housing, work, family, mobility and health, and to visit the areas you are considering before deciding.
